rationale: C06 plausibly supplied the child’s compact congressional-legislation letter template: identify attached material describing proposed legislation, urge enactment, explain the harm that persists unless legislation is enacted, and demand prompt congressional action. C07 independently shares the same congressional addressees and the distinctive urgency construction that only congressional action now will achieve the stated objective, but it lacks the child’s attachment-based opening. C18 has an accompanying Defense Department communication and implementation request, but its administrative purpose and structure are less similar.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The attached letter, addressed to me by the Secretary of Defense, reviews the serious nature of the personnel situation ... [and] outlines the major legislative proposals
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Attached is a draft of legislation which would extend certain benefits to persons who shall have served in the Armed Forces
shared_material.explanation: Both open by directing congressional recipients to attached material concerning armed-forces legislation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I urge that this legislation be enacted.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I hope the Congress will take favorable action on this legislation
shared_material.explanation: Both make a direct presidential request for congressional enactment.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Only when we have created a career military service ... will we be able to stop the wasteful losses
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Unless and until such legislation is enacted, certain individuals ... will be denied medical and hospital care.
shared_material.explanation: Both justify enactment through a conditional statement identifying a continuing military-personnel harm that legislation would remedy.
The closing urgency language is closely parallel and serves the same drafting function.
